description.narrative:
The escalation of armed conflict along the border has intensified humanitarian needs across seven provinces. Despite international appeals for a ceasefire, active fighting points have increased, forcing the relocation of major displacement sites such as Wat ThmorKambo camp near Samrong town and O’Ampel primary school camp in Anlong Veng. Shelling now poses a direct threat to displaced populations, compounding insecurity and instability.
The displacement of 55,743 families (192,173 people) has overwhelmed existing safetycentres. Vulnerable groups—including 58,603 women and 21,974 children—face heightened risks of inadequate shelter, food insecurity,poor sanitation, and limited access to safe water. The closure of 909 schools has disrupted education for 216,107 students, undermining children’s protection and psychosocial well-being. Current humanitarian assistance, while commendable, remains insufficient to meet the scale of urgent needs. Without a coordinated and adequately resourced response, displaced communities will continue to facedeteriorating living conditions, increased health risks, and loss of dignity.
The escalation of displacement has placed immense pressure on existing water and sanitation facilities in camps and safety centers. Immediate WASH interventions are critical to preventoutbreaks of waterborne diseases and maintain dignity among affected populations. Oxfam is preparing a response plan structured in two phases to ensure both immediate relief and sustained support for displaced communities. The first phase—Immediate Response— focuses on life saving interventions such as the provision of emergency shelter, safe drinking water, sanitation facilities, hygiene kits, and essential non food items. These actions are designed to stabilize conditions in camps and relocation sites, reduce health risks, and protect the dignity of affected families. The second phase—Medium Term Response— will build on emergency efforts by supporting transitional shelters, strengthening WASH infrastructure, and restoring livelihoods as people return to their homes once a ceasefire is declared and the situation has stabilized. This phased approach ensures that urgent humanitarian needs are met while laying the foundation for recovery, resilience, and longer term community stability.
With the purchase of sustaining living conditions andsafeguard health, Oxfam plans to support the following: Immediate Response: • Emergency Water Supply - Rapid deployment of safe drinking water to prevent dehydration and waterborne diseases: o Install 10 additional water filtration systems o Provide100 mobile 2000L water tanks in high-density camps. o Provide 10,000 of 20L water containers o Work with camps authorities to ensure daily provision of safe drinking water to displaced families. • Sanitation and Hygiene Facilities: Establish latrines, bathing facilities, and hygiene kits to reduce disease outbreaks. o Provide 100 mobile toilets. o Provide 200 portable cloth changing tents for women and girls o Provide 10,000 dignity kits (Soap, detergent, sanitary pads, nail-clipper, flash lights, medicated balm, mosquito nets) • Shelters: Provide temporary housing to protect families from exposure and insecurity - 10,000 plastic sheets for roofing, floor and wall The grant from OHK is to contribute to the overall implementation of the general immediate response plan.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project#s implementation.
